newsitem.title: USA: Dow slides 94 points, pounded by sell programs.
newsitem.headline: Dow slides 94 points, pounded by sell programs.

text.p: The Dow industrials finished sharply lower on Thursday, staggered by a wave of late sell programs that wiped out the blue chips' first foray over the 6900 mark.
The Dow slid 94 points to close unofficially at 6756 after dropping nearly 150 points in the last two hours of trading on volume that approached record levels.
The sudden turnaround was the direct product of a rapid sequence of sell programs apparently triggered by developments in the futures market.

At the height of the session's rally, just as the Dow was surpassing the 6900 mark for the first time in its history, the futures contract on the Standard & Poor's 500 index was also nearing a key psychological level, said Mike Rothberg, managing director of portfolio trading at Cantor Fitzgerald.
"The contract got to an all-time high and was headed for 800," Rotheberg said. "It hit 799.70 but couldn't break through, and right after it turned around we had sell programs."
Hit hardest were many of the stocks that had paced the Dow's seemingly unstoppable run toward 7000.

General Electric Co fell three points to 104-3/8 and Exxon Corp slid 3-1/2 to 102-3/4. International Business Machines Corp suffered its second straight day of heavy losses, skidding 5-5/8 to 151-3/4.

"This was more than profit-taking," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "These could be construed as major reversals particularly because they were on such heavy volume."
Still, even after the sell-off, share prices are much higher than where they were at the start of the year, he noted.
"The caveat is that these stocks had massive runs before today," he said.
Ironcially, the selling came as reports emerged that investment strategist Elaine Garzarelli had turned bullish on U.S. stocks, reversing her call for a 10 to 15 percent correction.
Garzarelli could not be reached for comment, but some on Wall Street said there was cause for concern if she had become the most recent convert to the bull camp.
"When the bears start to capitulate, that's a worrisome sign for the market," said Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management.
There were a handful of issues that bucked the trend, generally on the strength of earnings news.
United Technologies Corp gained 3-1/8 to 69-5/8 and Texaco Inc rose 1-3/8 to 108-3/8 after both reported quarterly results that pleased Wall Street.
PepsiCo Inc jumped 2-1/2 to 34-1/2 in extremely heavy volume that exceeded 30 million shares.
After the close, PepsiCo announced plans to spin off its restaurant businesses. Speculation that such a move was under consideration had swept the stock higher during the session.

Texas Instruments Inc surged seven points to 70-3/4. The company reported a fourth-quarter loss but investors focused instead on the improving outlook for its core semiconductor business and the company's agreement to sell its notebook computer unit to Taiwan-based Acer Inc.
Vanstar Corp tumbled 7-1/4 to 14-7/8 after warning that its third-quarter earnings would fall short of estimates.
Alex. Brown later lowered its rating on Vanstar to neutral from strong buy.
The S&P 500 index fell 8.67 to 777.56.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 9.69 to 1378.37.
On the New York Stock Exchange, declining issues outnumbered advancing issues by a 14-to-11 margin on record volume that exceeded 683.8 million shares.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
